title: This is what AI tools for Unity can do now. I vibe coded this FPS game. What do you think?
author: PigeonMaster2000
selftext: I created this game with an AI tool that I'm building. It's called Nimble Fox. You can play the game on your browser on [itch.io](https://nimblefox.itch.io/arctic-warfare).

replies.author: PigeonMaster2000
replies.body: Thanks! The heavy lifting was done by Nimble Fox: assets, code, pictures, sounds, music & particles were all made with AI automatically. There are still quite many limitations with this tool though. For example, placing objects on the correct locations, painting and crafting terrain as well as making small tweaks to have the game feel "just right" needed to be done manually in this game. The assets (including rigging and building bones) were automatically generated. Even still, sometimes you do need to prompt it a couple of times to get the result you were looking for.

replies.author: superkickstart
replies.body:
I guess it's a question of previous experience, skills and what your needs and requirements are. If you don't know how assets are actually made for to be animated or rendered properly, then i understand that you think that ai generated stuff can be good enough.

And if that's enough for your project, then that's fine. I'm trying to use ai tools as much as possible to speed up things and so that i can focus on design and actually making the game. It has already made me an expert in design and coding and hugely improved my art creation process. Unfortunately assets like models are still lacking when you need proper topology and detail level for animation, facial details, swappable clothes, tiling systems etc. 

Also keeping different models consistent with each others and the game's art direction is a nightmare. Right now the generation services like meshy just aren't up to the task and overpromise and in many cases, simpy lie about their capabilities.

That said, I'm sure this will improve in the future. Generators can output useful stuff for prototyping, sketching or maybe base models for example, but the work required to make these actually useful and production ready is still massive and the ai tools are in many cases doing more harm than good.

replies.author: ZHName
replies.body:
The market has already accepted messy models as "good enough" just as people have already fully adopted ai voiceover youtube video style. It's not perfect, but it works and the market dictates.

Regarding prototyping, I no longer need a 3d modeller. I no longer need a texture artist. Meshy or hunyuan-3d are more than sufficient and vibe coding a 3d game will become trivial for the consumer.

 Assets like models have still a long way to go, and I hope they get better and people just don't accept the current slop as the norm. For prototyping, sketching, and base models, it's mostly fine, but I'd have to dial back the quality and consistency significantly if I'd  just purely use generators. Ai can actually slow down and make things harder if you know how these are actually made and want to keep the same level of requirements and quality.
